blocks.content: Team: Consultify
Members: Fatima, Kseniia
Repository: https://github.com/ksublo/consultation_reservation_system
The repository is currently private.

items: Domain: university teacher consultation slot reservations.
Resource: a specific consultation slot.
Reservation: student, selected slot, title and description of the reason, and status.
User: a student creates a reservation; a teacher creates slots and approves or cancels reservations.
States: PENDING, CONFIRMED, CANCELLED.
Operations: create a slot and reservation, approve, cancel, and check availability.
Common rule: two active reservations cannot exist for the same slot; both PENDING and CONFIRMED block the slot.
Domain rule: a slot can only be created on weekdays between 07:15 and 19:15. A student can have at most five pending reservations.
System boundary: Notification Service (still in development).
Monorepo with frontend/ and backend/ folders.
Frontend: React, TypeScript and Vite.
Backend: Java 21, Spring Boot and Maven.
Persistence: PostgreSQL and Flyway migrations.
README and documentation in docs/ exist; the repository is ready for shared work.

blocks.content: The complete Project Frame is filled in docs/intent-and-change.md. It describes the system purpose, roles, concepts, persistent state, operations, reservation state transitions, business rules, Notification Service, assumption and an open question.
Category: C — Changeability.
Future change: a teacher will be able to reject a reservation with a reason. A REJECTED state will be added and the slot will become available to other students again.
This is relevant because the change affects the state model, history, business rules and frontend.

Tasks follow the team workflow. One team member implements a change in their own branch, another member reviews it in a pull request, and the change is merged into main after approval. The review verifies functionality, readability, project rules and conflicts.

We verified real reservation persistence in PostgreSQL. Docker Compose runs the database, backend and frontend; Flyway creates the schema and demo data at startup. The backend reads slots through the REST API and data can be verified in the database.

Result: availability is protected by both the backend and database constraints, so two active reservations cannot exist for the same slot.

The application already supports creating reservations, displaying available slots, teacher approval and reservation cancellation. Below is an overview of the completed code and the documentation we still need to finish.
Shared rules are defined in the Domain rules section below. Individual operations only reference them.

A student selects an available teacher slot, enters the consultation title and description, and submits a request. The system creates a PENDING reservation, blocking the slot for other students before the teacher confirms it.

Goal / user value:
A student requests a consultation for a specific teacher slot.

Trigger:
A signed-in student submits the selected consultation slot, title and description.

Observable requirement:
REQ-01: The system creates one PENDING Reservation for an existing active future slot if the domain rules are satisfied.

Preconditions:
- The student exists and is allowed to create a reservation.
- The slot exists, is ACTIVE and starts in the future.

Successful outcome:
- One new Reservation exists.
- Reservation.status = PENDING.
- A CREATED record is stored in reservation_history.

State transition:
[none] → PENDING

Domain rules / invariants:
BR-02 Slot exclusivity; BR-04 Slot and student rules.

Main success scenario:
1. The student submits the slot, title and description.
2. The system checks the student, slot and relevant rules.
3. The system stores a PENDING Reservation.
4. The system stores CREATED history and returns 201 Created with the identifier and status.

Alternative / failure outcomes:
- Unknown student or slot → rejected; no reservation is created.
- Inactive, past or already blocked slot → rejected; no reservation is created.
- PENDING limit exceeded or overlapping student slots → rejected; no reservation is created.

Verification examples:
- Active future slot + valid student → one PENDING reservation.
- Already blocked slot → rejected.
- Student with an overlapping active reservation → rejected.

Rationale / source:
The student expresses interest in a consultation; the teacher then decides whether to confirm or cancel it.
The calendar and API show only active future slots without a pending or confirmed reservation. This operation only reads data and makes no changes.

Goal / user value:
Students and teachers can see which consultation slots are available to reserve.

Trigger:
A user opens the calendar or requests available slots through the API.

Observable requirement:
REQ-02: The system returns an ACTIVE future slot as available only if it has no PENDING or CONFIRMED Reservation.

Preconditions:
- The request works with existing consultation slots.

Successful outcome:
- A list of available slots is returned.
- Neither Reservation nor ConsultationSlot is changed.

State transition:
None.

Domain rules / invariants:
BR-01 Interval semantics; BR-02 Slot exclusivity.

Main success scenario:
1. The user requests available slots.
2. The system selects ACTIVE future slots.
3. The system excludes slots blocked by PENDING or CONFIRMED reservations.
4. The system returns the remaining available slots.

Alternative / failure outcomes:
- Past slot → not returned as available.
- CANCELLED slot → not returned as available.
- PENDING or CONFIRMED reservation → slot is not returned as available.

Verification examples:
- ACTIVE future slot without a reservation → available.
- Slot with a PENDING reservation → unavailable.
- Slot with a CONFIRMED reservation → unavailable.

Rationale / source:
Users need to select only slots that cannot result in a reservation conflict.
A teacher confirms a pending reservation for their own slot in the request list. Only the slot owner may change PENDING to CONFIRMED.

Goal / user value:
A teacher accepts a pending request as a confirmed consultation.

Trigger:
A teacher chooses to confirm a specific PENDING reservation for their own slot.

Observable requirement:
REQ-03: The system changes a Reservation from PENDING to CONFIRMED only when the action is performed by the teacher who owns the consultation slot.

Preconditions:
- The Reservation exists.
- Reservation.status = PENDING.
- The actor is the TEACHER who owns the slot.

Successful outcome:
- Reservation.status = CONFIRMED.
- The slot remains blocked.
- A CONFIRMED record is stored in reservation_history.

State transition:
PENDING → CONFIRMED

Domain rules / invariants:
BR-02 Slot exclusivity.

Main success scenario:
1. The teacher selects a pending request.
2. The system checks that the reservation exists, its status and slot ownership.
3. The system changes the status to CONFIRMED.
4. The system stores CONFIRMED history and returns the confirmed reservation.

Alternative / failure outcomes:
- Nonexistent reservation → rejected.
- Student or another teacher → 403 Forbidden.
- CONFIRMED or CANCELLED reservation → rejected; the status does not change.

Verification examples:
- Slot owner + PENDING → CONFIRMED.
- Another teacher + PENDING → 403.
- CANCELLED → rejected without changes.

Rationale / source:
Teachers must control which requests for their slots they confirm.

A student cancels their own reservation; a teacher may cancel a reservation for their own slot. Cancellation is allowed at least three hours before the start and changes the status to CANCELLED while preserving history.

Goal / user value:
An authorized student or teacher cancels an active future consultation.

Trigger:
A student cancels their own reservation or a teacher cancels a reservation for their slot.

Observable requirement:
REQ-04: The system changes a PENDING or CONFIRMED reservation to CANCELLED if an authorized actor cancels it at least three hours before the start.

Preconditions:
- The Reservation exists.
- Reservation.status is PENDING or CONFIRMED.
- The actor is the reservation's student or the teacher who owns the slot.
- currentTime is at least three hours before startsAt.

Successful outcome:
- Reservation.status = CANCELLED.
- The actor, cancellation note and cancelledAt are stored.
- A CANCELLED record is stored in reservation_history.
- The slot is no longer blocked.

State transition:
PENDING → CANCELLED or CONFIRMED → CANCELLED

Domain rules / invariants:
BR-03 Cancellation policy; BR-02 Slot exclusivity.

Main success scenario:
1. An authorized actor submits a cancellation request.
2. The system checks the status, authorization and time limit.
3. The system changes the status to CANCELLED and stores cancellation details.
4. The system stores CANCELLED history and returns the cancelled reservation.

Alternative / failure outcomes:
- Nonexistent reservation → rejected.
- Unauthorized actor → 403 Forbidden.
- Already CANCELLED → rejected without changes.
- Less than three hours before the start → rejected without changes.

Verification examples:
- Student cancels PENDING 4 hours before the start → CANCELLED.
- Teacher cancels CONFIRMED 3 hours before the start → CANCELLED.
- Cancellation 2 hours before the start → rejected.

Rationale / source:
Cancellation must release the slot and preserve a traceable history of the change.

Our consultation slot is an exclusive resource: a specific time slot can belong to only one active reservation at a time. These rules apply across Create, Check Availability, Confirm and Cancel and are not repeated within individual operations.

BR-01 — Interval semantics
Consultation slots use half-open intervals [start, end). One slot may therefore end exactly when the next begins without an overlap.

BR-02 — Exclusive Resource invariant
There must be no more than one active Reservation per consultation slot. In our system, both PENDING and CONFIRMED are active states that block the slot.

Reason: a student cannot obtain a slot that is already awaiting a teacher's decision or has been confirmed. The database protects this invariant with the one_active_reservation_per_slot unique index.

BR-03 — Cancellation policy
A PENDING or CONFIRMED Reservation may be cancelled by the student who created it or the teacher who owns the consultation slot. Cancellation is allowed if currentTime is at least three hours before startsAt.

Cancellation changes the status to CANCELLED; the Reservation is not physically deleted. cancelledAt, actor, an optional cancellation note and a reservation_history record are stored. A CANCELLED Reservation no longer blocks the slot.

BR-04 — Domain-specific rule from C01
A teacher may create a consultation slot only on weekdays between 07:15 and 19:15. A student may have at most five PENDING reservations and must not have a time overlap with another active reservation.

Reason: this rule reflects normal university consultation hours and protects teachers and students from scheduling conflicts.
The team confirmed for the final v0.2 baseline that PENDING remains a blocking state. Automated tests for adjacent [start, end) intervals have been added.

sections.title: 10. Consistency review and acceptance of baseline v0.1

blocks.content: The team jointly reviewed REQ-01 through REQ-04. The review focuses on observable behaviour rather than the choice of database or another technical solution.

items: Meaning: ACTIVE, PENDING, CONFIRMED, CANCELLED, future slots and the three-hour limit have the same meaning in the specification, API and UI.
Rationale: each requirement protects a specific value for a student or teacher; none merely prescribes an implementation.
Verifiability: each REQ has a success example and a rejection or boundary example with the expected status and HTTP outcome.
Concurrency: two parallel attempts to reserve the same slot must result in at most one active reservation.
Consistency: Create blocks a slot with PENDING, Approve only changes its status to CONFIRMED, and Cancel releases it again.
Uncertainty: notifications are outside the baseline, so they are neither a claim nor a condition of the operations.

blocks.content:
Specification Baseline v0.1
Scope: Create Reservation, Check Availability, Confirm Reservation, Cancel Reservation.
Approval: to be completed by the team during the joint review (date, names and commit/tag).
Verification sources: API response, stored Reservation status and reservation_history.

Baseline v0.2 adds an explicit teacher approval step. The application already implements this step through the Approve Reservation endpoint; PENDING represents a request awaiting the teacher's decision.

Changed condition:
A Reservation does not become CONFIRMED automatically after creation; the teacher must approve the request.

Affected parts:
Create produces PENDING; Availability treats PENDING as blocking; Confirm is implemented as Approve in the UI/API; the state and use-case views include the teacher's decision.

Unaffected parts:
Intervals [start,end), slot ownership, the cancellation rule and history remain unchanged because the change does not alter time semantics or the requirement to record changes.

Decision for the current v0.2:
All consultation slots require teacher approval. PENDING blocks the slot to prevent concurrent requests. Rejection and expiration are not implemented in this version and are explicitly a topic for the next change, rather than hidden behaviour.
Architectural driver for C03: the teacher's state-changing operation, history records and concurrency protection must remain consistent across the API and persistence.

Goal / user value:
A teacher decides whether to accept a pending request for their slot as a confirmed consultation.

Trigger:
A teacher chooses to approve a PENDING Reservation for their own consultation slot.

Observable requirement:
REQ-05: The system changes a PENDING Reservation to CONFIRMED only for the teacher who owns the slot.

Preconditions:
- The Reservation exists and has status PENDING.
- The actor is the TEACHER who owns the slot.

Successful outcome:
- Reservation.status = CONFIRMED.
- A CONFIRMED record is created in reservation_history.
- The slot remains blocked.

State transition:
PENDING → CONFIRMED

Main scenario:
1. The teacher selects a pending request.
2. The system checks ownership and the initial status.
3. The system stores CONFIRMED and the history record.
4. The API returns the updated reservation.

Failure outcomes:
- Another teacher or a student → 403.
- Nonexistent, CONFIRMED or CANCELLED reservation → no changes, 4xx.

Verification examples:
- Owner + PENDING → CONFIRMED.
- Another teacher + PENDING → 403.
- CANCELLED → rejected.

The running application demonstrates request creation, available-slot filtering, teacher approval and cancellation by an authorized actor. The status is verified through both the API response and PostgreSQL data.

items: Create: valid student and future ACTIVE slot → 201 and PENDING; occupied slot or limit violation → 409.
Availability: ACTIVE future slot without an active reservation → displayed; PENDING/CONFIRMED, past or cancelled slot → not displayed.
Approve: slot owner approves PENDING → CONFIRMED; unauthorized actor → 403.
Cancel: authorized actor at least 3 hours before the start → CANCELLED; less time or invalid status → 4xx without changes.

sections.title: A8. Question for the next design stage

rows: How can we ensure that approval always uses the identity of the signed-in user?
The check currently uses the ID sent by the client. The test described in A3 confirmed that this check can be bypassed.
Only the slot owner may decide on its reservation.

blocks.content: AI helped locate the relevant code and prepare the diagram. We ran 9 API tests against the running application and also verified the results in the database:

rows: The owner approves a pending reservation.
HTTP 200. The reservation changed to CONFIRMED; the confirmation time, a history record and a student notification were stored.
Another teacher and a student send their own IDs (2 tests).
HTTP 403. Reservations, history and notifications remained unchanged.
The owner approves an already confirmed or cancelled reservation (2 tests).
HTTP 409. Reservations, history and notifications remained unchanged.
A nonexistent reservation or user specified in the request (2 tests).
HTTP 404. The test data remained unchanged.
Another signed-in teacher sends the owner's ID when approving.
HTTP 200. Another teacher's reservation was confirmed — the authorization bug was reproduced.
Another signed-in teacher sends the owner's ID when cancelling a pending reservation.
HTTP 200. Another teacher's reservation was cancelled — the same bug was reproduced here as well.

blocks.content: We used temporary accounts and reservations and removed them afterwards. The authorization bug is recorded in A3 and has not been fixed yet.

sections.title: Change from the original version — actor identity

blocks.content: Previously, approve/cancel trusted actorUserId from the request body. The controller now passes the authenticated session identity, and the reservation service checks the active role, ownership and allowed state. A supplied actor ID is ignored. The frontend sends only the token and an optional note for these actions.

Verification: all 10 regression tests passed. Another teacher or student cannot act using a spoofed ID (403, with no reservation, history or notification changes). The owner can approve a pending reservation, and its student or teacher can cancel it. Approval of CONFIRMED/CANCELLED returns 409; unauthenticated requests are rejected.

Tests exercise the real filter → API → service path with mocked persistence and session validation. They do not re-verify persistence or concurrency. ADR-01, the before/after comparison and details are in docs/architecture-and-decisions.md and docs/evidence-and-evolution.md. This fix covers reservation approval and cancellation; other endpoints require separate review.
